sources.title: Can I go to Australia?
sources.officialityEvidence: The Department of Home Affairs publishes this entry guidance on the Australian Government immi.homeaffairs.gov.au domain.
sources.supportingExcerpt: All other passport holders need the right visa to come to Australia. You also need to get your visa before you travel.

sources.title: Migration Act 1958, section 42: Visa essential for travel
sources.officialityEvidence: The Federal Register of Legislation publishes the current in-force Migration Act 1958 and identifies the Department of Home Affairs as administrator.
sources.supportingExcerpt: A non-citizen must not travel to Australia without a visa that is in effect.

sources.title: Visitor visa (subclass 600): Tourist stream (apply outside Australia)
sources.officialityEvidence: The Department of Home Affairs publishes this Visitor visa subclass portal on the Australian Government immi.homeaffairs.gov.au domain.
sources.supportingExcerpt: This visa stream lets you visit Australia as a tourist, to go on a cruise or to visit family and friends.

sources.supportingExcerpt: If you will be in Australia for less than 8 hours and you are not leaving the airport you may not need to apply.

policies.title: Ordinary passports outside Australia’s citizenship, SCV, ETA and eVisitor cohorts require an advance visa
policies.summary: For the listed ordinary passport holders travelling from outside Australia for tourism, cruises, or visits to family and friends, an appropriate Australian visa is required before travel. The Visitor visa (subclass 600) Tourist stream is the general visitor route; it is not a nationality-wide eVisa classification.
conditions: Scope is ordinary national passports and a visitor purpose: tourism, cruises, or visiting family and friends, with the traveller outside Australia when applying. It is not a grant or admission guarantee.

The listed cohort is the remaining 152 ordinary-passport codes after the separately researched Australian-citizen, New Zealand SCV, ETA subclass 601, and eVisitor subclass 651 cohorts; it does not reopen their document-specific exceptions.

An appropriate advance visa is required, but nationality alone does not establish a single subclass in every case. For this visitor purpose, the general route is the Visitor visa (subclass 600) Tourist stream; sponsorship, business, medical, study, work, or another purpose may require a different stream or visa.
A subclass 600 application may be lodged online and a granted visa is digitally linked to a passport. Those facts do not make the route a nationality-wide eVisa for this access taxonomy.

This cohort does not decide the position of a traveller who already holds a valid Australian visa, has Australian or New Zealand citizenship, residence or another immigration status, or is covered by a case-specific permission or exemption.

Transit is excluded: Transit Without a Visa, airport/transit-lounge conditions, a valid existing visa, and Transit visa (subclass 771) or Maritime Crew arrangements require separate route and document analysis.

Diplomatic, official, service, crew, refugee, stateless, non-citizen, certificate-of-identity, laissez-passer, and other special travel documents are outside this ordinary-passport nationality policy.

This does not displace relationship-based New Zealand routes. A non-New Zealand family member of a qualifying New Zealand SCV holder may instead be eligible for the New Zealand Citizen Family Relationship visa (subclass 461).
Health, character, identity, prior-visa, security, application-validity and border-entry requirements remain case-specific; Home Affairs may refuse a visa or entry.

application.label: Visitor visa (subclass 600) Tourist stream guidance
steps: Confirm that the journey is visitor travel rather than transit, crew, work, study, medical treatment, or another purpose.
Check for an existing Australian visa, citizenship, New Zealand SCV eligibility, a relationship-based route, or another case-specific status before choosing a visa.
If the Tourist stream is appropriate, apply from outside Australia and wait for written visa grant before travel.
